headline: Poliomyelitis in North Carolina in 1935
source: American Journal of Public Health and the Nation's Health
blurb: Carl V. Reynolds and J. C. Knox published a paper on polio in North Carolina in 1935, first read at a public health meeting in St. Louis in November 1935.

headline: Infectious Diseases
blurb: A 1939 North Carolina statute required all schoolchildren to be vaccinated against diphtheria.

headline: Polio in North Carolina
blurb: North Carolina's worst year for polio was 1948, when 2,516 cases and 143 deaths were reported.

headline: § 130A-152. Immunization required.
blurb: This North Carolina law says every child in the state must be immunized against diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough, polio, measles and rubella, and its history note starts with a 1957 act.

headline: Polio in North Carolina
blurb: In 1959, North Carolina became the first state to require that all children get the Salk polio vaccine.

headline: Notes from the Field: Measles Outbreak Associated with a Traveler Returning from India — North Carolina, April–May 2013
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: In April and May 2013, 23 measles cases in North Carolina were linked to an unvaccinated traveler who had returned from India, and 18 of the patients were unvaccinated.

headline: North Carolina Hepatitis A Outbreak Surpasses 1,000 Cases
source: North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services
blurb: North Carolina passed 1,000 reported hepatitis A cases tied to a national outbreak, with 63% of cases needing hospital care and 16 deaths.

headline: Whooping cough cases spike in N.C.
blurb: North Carolina had close to 600 reported whooping cough cases in 2024 by early December, far more than at the same point in 2023.
